Classify: false_positive (non-null proved by construction; non-actionable). `const before = (try Fuzzy.score(out[at], query, self.fuzzy_options)).?;` in `Suggestions.setItemsFuzzy` (src/component/suggestions.zig:97-160), site 135. Reusable invariant for this site: for every k < n, out[k] is an item that already returned non-null from Fuzzy.score with the SAME query and fuzzy_options. Source ranges: guard `const got = try Fuzzy.score(item, query, self.fuzzy_options) orelse continue;` at 131-132; read loop 133-137 with bound `at < n`; writes 138-143 (`out[at] = item; if (n < out.len) n += 1;`) plus the shift 141-142 which only propagates already-matched entries; n initialised to 0 at 120 and published as out[0..n] at 146. Every increment of n is preceded in the same iteration by writing a value that passed the line-132 guard, so inductively out[0..n] is a matched subset; n only ever grows by one and only after such a write, so the read at 135 never sees unwritten caller memory. Fuzzy.score is a pure function of (haystack, needle, fold_case) — no allocator, no state, no callback into caller code — so the second evaluation of a matched pair returns the identical non-null value; the documented doc says ties resolve to the leftmost alignment, making it deterministic (src/component/fuzzy.zig:97-99, 224-231). The `out` MUST NOT alias `items` precondition (suggestions.zig:84-85) is not load-bearing here: even under an aliasing violation every value ever written into out[0..n] is a `item` that matched, so the unwrap still holds. Caller path: any caller of setItemsFuzzy (all in-file tests: lines 411, 434, 453, 467, 473, 488, 504, 516, 523, 534, 543) passes a distinct result buffer, so the documented precondition holds in practice too. Optional, non-actionable: a TigerStyle-style `assert(Fuzzy.score(...).?)` style local assert or a comment at 135 would document the matched-subset invariant the reader must currently re-derive.
